details: 28 Oct: base-restores-only-four-keys-bench-s-relay-claud was built for nothing (4 agents, 7 min, a lane): master had fixed it on 25 Oct in 58d5d5f9, and the item exists only because `relay queue add --from <report> F<n>` queued a finding that a check had marked MET two minutes earlier (found by the review of that empty branch).
failing_case: A review report with F1 and a check record marking F1 MET: `relay queue add --from review.json F1` queues it.
pass_cases: The same refuses and names the check.
A finding marked NOT MET or not checked is still queued.
findings.summary: queue add --from queues a finding a check marked MET

details: CONFIRMED by measurement. bin/relay opens relay_git.reading() only at line 916, not around queue add, so stored_text and
is_ancestor fall back to one `git` subprocess each: one per check file per branch (each lane branch carries master's
432 records again, so the same blob is read up to 22 times). Principle 2 (waste): waste that repeats on every run is
MEDIUM and fixed before the merge. A person or agent running `relay queue add --from` waits nearly a minute.
evidence: sum of `git ls-tree --name-only <ref> .relay/checks/ | grep -c check.json$` -> 7288; on master -> 432
time python3 -I -c "... rq.met_in_a_check('/Users/amidman/relay', <probe review>, 'F1')"  -> None, 54.191 total
failing_case: On /Users/amidman/relay today (22 local branches, 7288 check.json files over them, 432 on master):
met_in_a_check(repo, <review.json>, "F1"), the call bin/relay:1102 makes through add_from outside relay_git.reading(),
takes 54.2 s (23.6 s user, 27.8 s sys). It runs on every `relay queue add --from`, and grows with each check and lane.
It should take a few seconds: the same call inside relay_git.reading() takes 2.9 s and returns the same answer.
fix_hint: Wrap the body of met_in_a_check (it only reads; no ref moves) in `with relay_git.reading():`. Optionally dedupe by blob id
(ls-tree without --name-only) so a record shared by several branches is parsed once.
pass_cases: 1. `relay queue add --from <report> F<n>` on a repo with N branches and many check records reads the check files without
one git process per file (e.g. a test that counts relay_git.git calls, or met_in_a_check run inside relay_git.reading()),
and returns the same answer as now.
2. The new test test_add_from_refuses_a_finding_a_later_check_marked_met_and_names_the_check still refuses and names the head.
4. add_from's own commit (the queue item) is made outside the reading window, since reading() is not for code that commits.
findings.summary: relay queue add --from now takes about 54 s on the live repo: every check file of every branch is read by its own git process

details: CONFIRMED by reading the tests: met_check always makes the review at the branch start, an ancestor of the check head, and
the "never checked" case uses a different file name, so neither exercises the ancestry condition. The collision itself is
rare today: measured 0 of 248 review file names on master's check records reused at a different sha. Matching on
f["since"] == reviewed (the record stores the review's sha per finding) would be exact, though a rebased review's since is
its twin, so keep the ancestry check as the fallback. Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: scan of master's .relay/checks/*.check.json: 248 review sources, 0 with more than one `since`
failing_case: Remove the `relay_git.is_ancestor(main, reviewed, record["head"])` condition from met_in_a_check: both new tests still
pass, so the guard against a same-named review of another branch is untested. With the guard, the match is still by file
name plus ancestry, not by the finding's own `since`: a review A made at R_A, merged, and a later review B of another
branch saved under the same file name (e.g. review-precheck.json) whose check marks F1 MET makes
`relay queue add --from A F1` refuse though A's F1 was never checked. It should queue it.
fix_hint: Add a test: same file name, reviewed not an ancestor of the check head -> queued. Optionally match on f["since"] == reviewed first.
pass_cases: 1. A check on wt/m marks F1 of review-m.json MET, but the review given to add_from has the same file name and a
`reviewed` sha that is not in the history of the check's head: add_from queues F1.
2. The same review whose `reviewed` equals the check finding's `since`: refused, naming the check (the current test).
reason: tests/test_queue.py:288 and :299 pass and encode the cases.
findings.summary: no test holds the guard that the check is built on the review's commit; a MET of another review of the same file name refuses
